chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers.'

He said: 'He means the orphans. When a man takes charge of orphans in his guardianship, he should spend from his own wealth for them according to their need, in proportion to what he spends for each of them, so that he mixes with them and they all eat together.'
And he should not deduct anything from their wealth; indeed, it is the Fire (for doing so).
ai.seo_question: How should a guardian spend on orphans to avoid consuming their wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'mixing' with orphans involves the guardian integrating them into his household and feeding them from his own resources, ensuring they eat together without the guardian deducting their share from the orphans' principal wealth. This distinction prevents the guardian from consuming the orphans' property, a practice the Imam warns is a path to the Fire, emphasizing the preservation of the orphans' capital while providing for their daily sustenance.
